newsitem.title: CANADA: CanOxy buys Gulf of Mexico blocks.
newsitem.headline: CanOxy buys Gulf of Mexico blocks.

text.p: Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd said on Tuesday that its Dallas-based subsidiary closed an acquisition of Gulf of Mexico offshore blocks from Shell Offshore Inc for US$50.2 million.

CanOxy said the purchase, made by CXY Energy Offshore Inc, included 100 percent interest in Vermilion Blocks 302, 321, 339 and 340, located in 200 feet of water about 80 miles from the coast of Louisiana.
The blocks contain two fields that are currently producing about 29 million cubic feet of natural gas and 325 barrels of oil and gas liquids per day from 14 wells and four platforms.

The fields, discovered in the 1970s, produce from multiple stacked sand reserviors and have produced over 370 billion cubic feet of gas and nine million barrels of oil and liquids to date, CanOxy said.
It said its technical staff had identified large potential for new drilling, workovers of existing wells and the addition of gas compression facilties.
"An aggressive exploitation program is planned for 1997," CanOxy said.
The Vermilion fields, which are 65 miles southwest of CanOxy's Eugene Island properties, "create a new core production area with substantial reserves and upside potential," it said.
